You should not see any change, as these things were long ago replaced with our Marketplace asset extensions, but just be aware that if you do still reference these in old projects, then you will need to remove that code now.
In-Game: Persistent objects now fire their Clean Up event after their Game End event when the runner is closed, like non-Persistent objects do

In-Game: pointer_null no longer always returns true if the string/number compared against starts with a 0 [note that pointers can only be compared successfully against other pointers - previous releases incorrectly appeared to allow comparisons with other types]

summary:
2.3.7 brings the ability to sign in to GMS2 using an Opera single sign-on account if you wish, adds support for a new "nullish" operator in your code, and introduces three more filter layer types your can use in your rooms as well as enabling the Inspector for use in your rooms. This release also sees several performance increases (such as native Mac M1 architecture support for GMS2 itself) and some load time boosts for opening your projects and also for games starting at the end of builds.

This release also raises Spine support to require v4.0. Please be aware this updated Spine runtime will require you to re-export your Spine images using v4.0 before they will work again in GMS2!

The matching runtime version updates a number of the SDKs GMS2 requires during builds (so please see our setup guides if you have issues building projects) and fixes an issue with Android API 31+ with Android 12 devices.

There are of course also a number of other changes and several important bug fixes, so of course do also read the rest of the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Tweaked the Renderer's Memory-management
changes: Should resolve a number of poor performance issues and graphics card memory crashes seen in the last couple of releases
If you do still have issues, please file a bug report, but remember to attach your ui.log and a DXDiag/System Information report

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: Marketplace/Local Package Integration: Packages downloaded to a Dropbox folder and imported whilst Dropbox is running will give "Failed to verify the package" error
Note: this one is actually because Dropbox is quietly adding a .device file into your downloads - you may wish to review any files you have downloaded already
Startup: [Mac IDE] GMS2 no longer crashes immediately when using Mojave

Note: A few tickets suggest newer OS versions would show the same issue if you're actually using old Mac hardware which Apple do not themselves support in that OS, but you have turned off SIP and installed anyway

changes: Asset Browser: Creating an asset via keyboard hotkey immediately after deleting a folder in the Asset Browser now adds the new asset correctly/safely, rather than causing an error next time you open that project
Building Projects: [YYC] A much more helpful error is now shown when builds fail because your Visual Studio install directory as set in Preferences cannot be found
Building Projects: Fixed a likely reason for "Unable to obtain permission to execute" shown to some users who have valid licences [also added more logging for if this issue does happen again]
General: [Ubuntu and Mac IDEs] Fixed an exception in Graphics.VertexBuffer.Destroy() when closing GMS2
Image Editor: Undoing a resize by "Resize All Frames" now undoes both of the changes to height and width properly
Image Editor: "Rotate brush 90 degrees" shortcut key now works again
Inspector: "Disable IDE transition animations" Preference is now obeyed by Inspector windows also
Preferences: [Mac IDE] Generating an Android keystore File now works on Macs with M1 CPUs

Preferences: "Auto Logout" might fail for some Edu customers when the network connection is not correct, so have we added more logging for this - if you are affected by this issue also, then please file a bug report and attach your ui.log

Room Editor: Cut/Copy/Paste Instance keyboard shortcuts are now working again
Sprite Editor: GMS2 can now import .jpg files made by Photoshop 2021 [could have affected other editors in their new versions also, as it's due to a change in the .jpg header]

Workspace Overview: You are again able to flow backwards (Shift+Tab whilst still holding Ctrl)
Workspace Overview: Ctrl+Tab now correctly selects the last active window in the list whenever you try to select that one

summary:
2.3.7 brings the ability to sign in to GMS2 using an Opera single sign-on account if you wish, adds support for a new "nullish" operator in your code, and introduces three more filter layer types your can use in your rooms as well as enabling the Inspector for use in your rooms. This release also sees several performance increases (such as native Mac M1 architecture support for GMS2 itself) and some load time boosts for opening your projects and also for games starting at the end of builds.

This release also raises Spine support to require v4.0. Please be aware this updated Spine runtime will require you to re-export your Spine images using v4.0 before they will work again in GMS2!

The matching runtime version updates a number of the SDKs GMS2 requires during builds (so please see our setup guides if you have issues building projects) and fixes an issue with Android API 31+ with Android 12 devices.

There are of course also a number of other changes and several important bug fixes, so of course do also read the rest of the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Introduced logging-in via Opera single sign-on
changes: You now have the choice of logging-in with your existing YoYo details or (particularly useful if you're working with the OperaGX target a lot) linking your Opera account to your YoYo Account and then using that to sign-in with

If you do not already have an Opera account, then you can create one from the licensing dialog. Once your account is created, the Opera site will send you to your YoYo Accounts page so that you can log in there one time and link the two accounts. After that, you will be able to sign-in to GMS2 using the Opera account each time.

groups.title: Added Ability To Omit Arguments On Function Calls
changes: Function calls can now be made with missing arguments, these are then passed as undefined and either optional arguments or the called function can handle that
I.e., you can now write MyFunctionCall(1,2,,,5) and get the same result as if you had written MyFunctionCall(1, 2, undefined, undefined, 5)

groups.title: Added Two New "Nullish" Operators
changes: Added a new ?? operator - called via code such as variable ?? expression - which checks to see if variable is either undefined or pointer_null, and if it is then it returns expression, otherwise it returns variable

Also added a matching assignment operator - called via code such as variable ??= expression - which will check variable to see if it is either undefined or pointer_null, and if is is then it will assign expression to variable, otherwise it does nothing

groups.title: Added the Room Instance Inspector
changes: Basic functionality of the Room Instance inspector has been added, and so you can now open this inspector from the Window menubar
At the moment this new inspector only applies to instances in your room and does not contain full functionality (for example, you cannot edit creation code yet)

groups.title: Added Several New Room Editor Filter Layer Types
changes: We have now added Heat Haze, Twirl Distort, and Underwater as filter options you can choose in the Room Editor
Note: The contents of the layer type dropdown does depend on which runtime is currently active, so you will only see these if using 2.3.7 runtimes
There are also some visual improvements to the Desaturate and Large Blur layers (this one also gains a room editor performance fix)

groups.title: Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds
changes: A while ago, we introduced a change where GMS2 assumes that a sound asset using an .ogg file type is already in the format you want and won't recompile the .ogg file if the Sound Editor's settings match a quick scan of contents of the .ogg

However, it is possible that you might want an individual sound to always ensure that it is compiled by GMS2 before it is added to your project cache folder, so we have now added an option for this into the Sound Editor
Be aware that this will force that sound to recompile each build, so you may wish to only tick this option when required

groups.title: Added ability to switch off the use of kerning for a font
changes: There is a new setting in the Font Editor for saying whether you wish to ignore the kerning information within the font

Note: a reminder that different fonts may legitimately need different interpreter versions to be used in the font editor's options for that font asset, so you might want to check these options first if you have issues with a font

groups.title: Updated Spine Support To Target v4.0
changes: Added support for importing and using Spine 4.0 images in your games
However, be aware that due to the way the Spine runtime only supports one version at a time, you will need to use Spine 4.0 to re-export all of your assets for your projects before they will work now
If you have any old-format Spine sprites in your project, then you will be shown an error for these when trying to build the game

groups.title: Implemented Android 12/API 31+ intent-filter changes
changes: This change fixes games crashing on startup if ran on an Android 12 device specifically when the game had been compiled using Android API 31+ (APIs 30 and older would be fine even if ran on Android 12)
Note: If you have any Android extensions in your projects be aware these may need fixes in order to support building with API 31+, as Google have introduced a number of changes
(We will be updating our Marketplace assets asap, so please check their web pages if you need the updated versions.)

groups.title: Changes to the Workspace Overview (Ctrl+Tab) window's control scheme
changes: Several "flow keys" such as Alt/Ctrl/Tab, etc., are now configurable if you wish - this can be done in Preferences > Redefine Keys

Partly because of this change, the Workspace Overview panel has now changed so that if you use a key combo which uses a flow key (such as the default of Ctrl+Tab), then you need to hold down the Ctrl like you always did in older versions of GMS2, but if you rebind the key combo to not use a flow key (e.g. just Tab), then you now do not need to keep holding down Tab to keep the window open

groups.title: Removed old advertising functions from autocomplete
changes: Removed a number of obsolete generic ads_...() functions we long ago replaced with provider-specific functions included in our Marketplace assets
Also removed a number of old ad provider-specific functions such as Supersonic and Playhaven
If you do still somehow refer to any of these old functions in your code, please remove the calls to them now

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: Asset Browser thumbnail images now load asynchronously and we have optimised this process also, so you should find that your projects now load faster/GMS2 is responsive sooner after the project has loaded (of course, projects with small numbers of images may not see much of a change here)
Note: If you do suddenly have any issues with loading your projects, please do report it asap (attaching the project)

We have further changed IDE rendering to reduce the amount of video memory allocated and to reuse this smaller amount rather than discarding and making new all the time - this should lower overall RAM usage a bit, but more importantly will stop a number of IDE crashes some users saw in 2.3.6 (particularly when using Intel integrated GPUs)
Fixed an SSO licensing refresh to be the correct once-a-month, so you will now be logged-out far less often if using SSO
Fixed that Local and Marketplace Packages were being merged if an older package exists at your chosen save location, rather than the old one deleted first
Note: There was a related Web fix made recently to stop packages being invalid when downloaded again inside GMS
Updated our versions of SDL (input/output) and FNA (the renderer) again, so that we gain a numer of IME improvements and other stability fixes
The Mac IDE now runs natively on an M1 CPU-equipped Mac, rather than using the Rosetta compatibility layer, which should improve performance and stability - any issues, let us know!
Sounds/Sprites are now immediately updated and saved when their audio/texture group is renamed, so do factor this into your workflow when editing these types of assets

changes: This change fixes games crashing on startup if ran on an Android 12 device specifically when the game had been compiled using Android API 31+ (APIs 30 and older would be fine even if ran on Android 12)
Note: If you have any Android extensions in your projects be aware these may need fixes in order to support building with API 31+, as Google have introduced a number of changes
(We will be updating our Marketplace assets asap, so please check their web pages if you need the updated versions)

groups.title: Added Ability To Forcibly Recompile Individual Sounds
changes: This runtime adds support for the new "Always Convert" functionality for sounds in the 2.3.7 IDE (see the IDE notes for more info)

groups.title: Added Several New Filter Layer Types
changes: This runtime adds support for three new Room Editor filter layer types in the 2.3.7 IDE - Heat Haze, Twirt Distort, and Underwater (see the IDE notes for more info)

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: In-Game: Stopped Ogg playback using existing channels that are still active, but no longer playing their previous sound and so are currently closing

Note: This fixes issues with sound playback using the wrong settings (e.g., the new sound looping when it's not meant to or being unable to fade it out) or with audio_get_name() failing to be able to tell what the currently-playing sound is, but you should check any audio-intensive projects carefully
Doing a "Create Exe" for Opera GX will now always use PNGCrush to compress all your images and reduce the submission package size
Note: This will ensure your project's build cache is recreated for all images first (and does so every Create Exe), so be aware that build times will be a little longer now
True and False are now actual booleans (so therefore typeof(true) will return "boolean" and is_bool(true) will return 1, etc.)

Made a significant optimisation for runner loading times if your project has lots of objects in it (typically >1000 before you will see real improvements) - this improvement is greater still if physics is enabled or if lots of the objects have collision events

groups.title: Other Bugs Fixed
changes: Building Projects: [Ubuntu ARM] Fixed a suffix name clash error when your project contains extensions for both armv7 and aarch64
Building Projects: [HTML5] Code "static a=[]; static b=1" no longer produces invalid JS
Building Projects: [iOS] Fixed building projects when using Xcode 13
Extensions: Adding an int64 to a dsmap from an extension no longer converts the value to a double first
Garbage Collection: Fixed a game crash when assigning a function literal to a global variable in GML extension's init function
In-Game: Moving a particle system to another layer no longer also moves the Object it was created by
In-Game: Shake filters no longer cause tiles on lower layers to briefly disappear when the filter starts playing
In-Game: Made a few appearance/quality fixes for the Twirl Distort filter
In-Game: "ref" variable inside weak_ref now returns undefined if the reference has been GC'ed
In-Game: [Windows] Windows' error sound effect no longer plays when using Alt+Enter to toggle fullscreen
In-Game: [Windows] Fixed a memory leak for window "handles" which caused their count to keep increasing
In-Game: [macOS] Precise collisions now work correctly for rotated sprites again [a collisions optimisation fix had been lost for 2.3.6, but has now been restored]
In-Game: [Ubuntu] Fixed a crash on game start if using any functions from .gml extensions in the project
In-Game: [OperaGX] Fixed a crash on game start if using any Included Files pointing to external WASM packages
In-Game: [OperaGX] Implemented client-side game caching within the browser
In-Game: [HTML5] Fixed game crashes when attempting to destroy an instance twice, if that instance has code for handling a ds list
In-Game: [HTML5] You are now able to convert a function to a boolean [which fixes an uncaught exception in earlier releases]
In-Game: [HTML5] Fixed a crash when deleting a physics joint
In-Game: [HTML5] Instances in the process of being destroyed are no longer found or will return values when calling "ObjectName.variableName" code, so now works the same as other platforms
In Game: [HTML5] Spine animations now work properly again / In-Game: [HTML5] draw_skeleton_time() now works again
In-Game: [HTML5] Intersect View Boundary events now correctly stop firing after the object has left the view, so now works the same as other platforms
In-Game: [Android VM and YYC] Fixed an inconsistency with the contents of a struct when ran on these two targets
In-Game: [Android] Accessing a "global." array no longer gives unexpected "trying to index a variable not an array" error

In-Game: [OperaGX] audio_position_listener() no longer causes audio skipping if called frequently in a Step event [assuming you don't actually move the listener every frame, as now subsequent calls to set the same position are ignored]
In-Game: buffer_compress(oldBufffer,newBuffer) no longer blocks memory being freed by a subsequent call to buffer_delete(oldBuffer)
In-Game: display_get_frequency() fixed/reimplemented this old function so it now works with modern monitors and devices

In-Game: draw_sprite_stretched() and draw_sprite_stretched_ext() no longer obey origin offset values when drawing nine slice sprites, so behave the way the manual says they should have and the same as non-nine slice sprites did
In-Game: [HTML5] draw_tile() will now draw the expected tiles if called inside a "with(structName)" block
In-Game: [HTML5] environment_get_variable() now returns an empty string instead of "undefined", so now works the same as other platforms

In-Game: json_decode() no longer fails for strings containing more than 32 layers of nested items [the new limit is 128]

summary:
2.3.6 introduces a new design to the Start Page and the concept of Template projects (which you can turn your own projects into if you wish), plus support for a new Filters layer in the Room Editor which allows you to quickly and easily add special effects into your games! As well as the new things, it brings a lot of stability fixes (in the IDE and in-game), such as changing the default renderer on Windows to Direct3D and stopping a fair number of crashes throughout the IDE.

In-game, it fixes a number of issues with precise collisions (especially with scaled-up small sprites) on all targets and also resolves a number of issues with the new OperaGX target we released in 2.3.5, so now your OperaGX games can do more and will work better.

Please note there is also a bit of clean-up of old code and variable/event names, so please see the important changes section below in case any of this applies to you and so you now need to tweak your code slightly.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes, so of course do also read the rest of the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Changed the renderer used for the Windows IDE
changes: The Windows IDE now uses Direct3D rather than the OpenGL it used in all previous releases

You should see that this release fixes many of the rendering issues that have been reported for various editors in the last couple of GMS2 releases, plus likely an improvement to performance (especially if you had very poor performance in the last few releases)

groups.title: Redesigned the Start Page
changes: This version includes our new-look Start Page, complete with a quick UI tutorial aimed at new-users (for experienced users, you can skip and disable seeing it again)
Our demo projects are now "Templates" on the new project screen, ready to be used as the basis of your own projects

You are also now able to turn your own projects into Templates so you can reuse them as the base of new projects later on - see the new File > Export > As a Template and the matching settings in Game Options for doing this
Note that the Home button on the menubar now closes your current project and returns you to the Start Page, ready to start working on a different project, so do be aware of this workflow change

groups.title: Added support for Filters and Effects in the Room Editor
changes: Indie and Enterprise users now have early access to the new "Filters and Effects" feature, which allows easily adding one of a range of graphical effect layers into your rooms
Simply create a new Filter layer, use the dropdown to set which filter to use, and the layer then applies your chosen filter to all other layers at a lower depth
These filters are even previewable in the Room Editor and so will automatically show you your end result (there is a new menubar option to disable Room Editor previews if you don't want this)

groups.title: Added a Key Conflicts window to the Redefinable Keys menu
changes: A new conflict window is now presented in the event of you trying to use the same keys for commands which would disrupt each other
This window provides suggested alternatives and lets you easily see other uses of those keys

groups.title: Removed old-format "..._name()" functions from autocomplete
changes: We have removed the old object/sprite/font/path/timeline_name() function definitions in the runner, as these were replaced with ..._get_name() a long time ago, and so autocomplete has been accidentally showing "duplicates" for a little while
If you still refer to these old-style names in your code, please change to calling the correct name now

Undo operations have been improved, so you should now observe fewer unexpected behaviours and more stability
Fixed a bug with custom keybinding remaps not always saving correctly if you are using the Mac IDE
Removed the ev_async_message_event constant used with event_perform_async(), as this event didn't fire Broadcast Message events like some users were attempting to use it for, and so caused confusion
Note: if you have this code in your project now, please change it to a suitable alternative event

summary:
2.3.5 brings a lot of stability fixes and continues the improvements to the product enabled by the new renderer and input/output systems introduced in 2.3.4. However, we also enabled the Inspector within the Sprite Editor, added new UI in Preferences to allow you to redefine the hotkeys GMS2 uses throughout the product, and introduced several other small quality-of-life tweaks which you can read about below.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes, so please do read the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Sprites Inspector
changes: The Inspector has now been enabled for Sprites also, giving you the option of trying this new workflow in another editor - please do let us know how you find using it
A reminder that the Inspector currently still has to be enabled manually from the Windows option on the menubar

groups.title: Redefinable Keys Support
changes: We have now added the ability for you to change GMS2's hotkey combinations for various commands throughout the IDE
See the new Preferences > Redefine Keys section for controlling this

groups.title: UX Tweak For The Create Exe Process
changes: Added a new Preference to always silently stop any existing run when clicking to create an executable, and then carry on with the new build as normal
Note this defaults to "off" (so you won't see any change) and you can enable it via Preferences > General Settings > Compiling > "Automatically stop running before packaging"

groups.title: Startup Tweak For Web Server Port Check
changes: Instead of checking your webserver port every startup, GMS2 will now only check this at the time you actually try to start the webserver (e.g., running a HTML5 game or opening the manual if the Preference to use the local manual is actually enabled)

Note you would still see the dialog at these times if your port remains blocked, so you should continue to see our Permissions FAQ for more info on how to fix this, as GMS2 will not create firewall rules for you

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: Asset Browser: [2.3.5] Removed the restriction on included files with names beginning with a number, as this is no longer required on current Apple OS versions [be careful claiming backwards support, though]

Game Options: Android's product information fields no longer allow you to type in hyphens, as we have had tickets from a few users who had typed this and caused Gradle to error when building the project
Note: If your project already has hyphens in any of these three text fields, please remove them now, as otherwise your build will fail
Project Load: Added more logging for "completely empty ID reference" errors and also a fix to more reliably tell you the name of the asset(s) affected, so that you can fix your projects more easily
Note: If you have a project which has this issue, please back it up first, but then do try it in this version and to attempt to fix your issue - if you are unable, send us the backup in a ticket

Project Save: Fixed a versioning issue which meant importing a 2.3.4-format extension into 2.3.3 and then deleting the extension in the Asset Browser deletes the entire project [2.3.5 will now export files safe to use in those old IDEs]

groups.title: Other Bugs Fixed
changes: Asset Browser: [Mac IDE] Ctrl+Click now works again in the Asset Browser and brings up the context menu as expected
Building Projects: Games now run if launched from the IDE in Linux distros which use Wayland windowing system (e.g.: Ubuntu 21 / Chrome 90)
Building Projects: Non-Latin characters can now be used in filenames when creating a .zip package
Code Editor: Made a fix for multi-column text insertion when using an IME input system

Code Editor: [Mac IDE] Added Cmd+G again as a hotkey for opening Go To Line (Ctrl+G worked already)
Code Editor (DnD): Dragging a script into an "Execute Script" node now actually assigns it to the node, rather than just opening it elsewhere
Code Editor: Accidentally adding double brackets when calling a function no longer gives a large parser error tooltip in the gutter
Code Editor: Fixed user-defined shortcuts for code snippets being broken in 2.3.4
Code Editor: [Mac IDE] Undo will no longer modify multiple lines if a mouse click was used to move the caret to a different line, rather than Enter
Debugger: Stepping code functionality no longer navigates in some circumstances to a line that is not actually getting called
Debugger: Fixed the Reset Layout menubar command so it actually removes your layout file and therefore resets your layout
Image Editor: [Mac IDE] Cutting a frame no longer causes two frames to be cut
Image Editor: [Mac IDE] Copy-pasting a frame no longer pastes it twice
Image Editor: Fixed that typing in a number for a new Brush Size instead selected the corresponding frame of your sprite
Image Editor: Fixed issues when drawing with the Polygon tool which could cause various bits of the screen to draw incorrectly
Image Editor: Fixed that red/blue were swapped when pasting-in from external applications and that alpha was also wrong when copy/paste inside GMS2 itself
Image Editor: Colour Replace tool now uses the correct red/blue values, like the fix above
Image Editor: Fixed GMS2 going unstable when using the Colour Picker tool
Image Editor: Layers are no longer incorrectly added to sub-groups after reopening the project
Inspector: [Tile Set] Fixed GMS2 going unstable when centre-fitting a preview of an empty Tile Set
Inspector: [Tile Set] The preview area now shows the usual checkerboard to represent empty Tile Sets
Install: Setting your installer language to Brazilian Portuguese or Russian now correctly changes the initial IDE language to be the same
Install: Cleaned the Windows installer of any no-longer-used "components" packages for old versions of .NET and Visual C Runtime
Project Load: Fixed GMS2 crashing when converting old-format (1.4 or 2.2.5) projects if you have certain newer targets on your licence
Project Load: Made GMS2 more reliably able to load some corrupted projects and therefore recover as much as possible
Project Save: GMS2 no longer goes unstable after importing some assets which use room inheritance from Local Packages and then deleting those assets
Project Save: Resources created in the root of a project and then immediately moved into a group now save correctly again
Project Save: GMS2 now automatically removes trailing whitespace in asset names rather than showing a filename error about the unwanted space character
Sprite Editor: You can no longer resize the first frame into a negative value - fixes a minor UI issue with the editor not handling this properly and updating the time bar
Startup: Added more logging to track down a rare startup crash "You must write ContentLength bytes to the request stream before calling [Begin]GetResponse" in the ui.log
Startup: Added a fix for the Mac IDE getting an error about not being able to download and install Mono (it says a runtime could not be installed, but this was the Mono installer itself)
Startup: Now only checks if the manual port is open if Preference to use the local manual is actually enabled [see the info in the section for this above]
UI/UX: GMS2 is no longer able to create multiple Confirm Quit dialogs (it will just reuse the one), which stops an odd crash from happening
UI/UX: Made a fix for ignoring all shortcuts when focus is in a text editor - now correctly handles suitable shortcuts again (e.g., Ctrl+S to save your project)
UI/UX: Cmd+T and Ctrl+T now function properly again
Workspaces: Fixed that dragging a workspace out to become a new desktop was moving the new window in the wrong direction for that initial drag

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: Building Projects: Android/iOS extensions with existing injection code made in 2.3.3-or-older no longer require editing one time before they will build properly
In-Game: buffer_seek() is no longer required after async_load[? "buffer"] - the async_load puts the buffer back to the correct starting position as it used to

groups.title: Other Bugs Fixed
changes: Building Projects: Fixed that games did not run from the IDE if the target machine is a Linux distro using Wayland windowing system (e.g., Ubuntu 21 / Chrome 90)
Building Projects: [Mac IDE] Ubuntu builds should no longer fail due to ssh connection "already connected" error regarding the log file being missing
Building Projects: [Ubuntu IDE] Local runs/debugging games should now find the correct real display even when third-party apps have created multiple virtual displays
Debugger: Fixed stepping code functionality so it will no longer in certain circumstances navigate to a line that is not actually getting called
In-Game: Fixed object parameters in functions not working as expected after destroying and recreating an instance of that object
In-Game: Fixed some inconsistent scoping behaviours of same-struct variable access which was introduced in 2.3.4
In-Game: Fixed an "Unset" error when referencing instance variables via object_id
In-Game: Collision masks now scale correctly to match nine-slice scaling
In-Game: Precise collisions no longer cause the significant performance drop seen in 2.3.4
In-Game: asset_get_index() can now get the index of Scripts [HTML5]
In-Game [HTML5] draw_* functions' behaviour when alpha is set to 255 is now consistent with Windows
In-Game: file_rename() now works when specifying a non-ASCII path
In-Game: tag_get_asset_ids() now returns the correct values for Scripts [HTML5]
Ticket: [HTML5] Cicla... no longer crashes on array_sort()
Ticket: [HTML5] "html5 return self" project now works on HTML5
Ticket: [Windows] Fixed silent crashes when starting project CryptoS...
Ticket: [YYC] Fixed silent crashes in lds-yyc-crash when creating a custom struct and performing functions, unless show_debug_message() was called first

summary:
2.3.4 changes a lot of the underlying systems for input/output and how the IDE is rendered, allowing us to fix some longstanding differences Windows IDE vs Mac IDE and also to better support modern input devices and new OSes going forward. You may not notice much change and this might look like a small release, but there have been a lot of changes, fixes and improvements made throughout the IDE.

There is also an overhaul in the versions of Visual Studio now required. Almost all platforms which used VS2015 before now require Visual Studio 2019, so please ensure you install this if you haven't already and also check your GMS2 Preferences paths are now correct, otherwise you will have errors when building YYC platforms/UWP/consoles. More information and a link to the Required SDKs can be found further down this page or on the Help menu inside GMS2 itself.

We also squeezed in two new console exports - Microsoft Xbox Series X/S and Sony PlayStation 5! If you are already approved for consoles these will appear in Target Manager as normal.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes, so please do read the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

You may not notice much change and this might look like a small release, but there have been a lot of changes, fixes and improvements made throughout the IDE.

There is also an overhaul in the versions of Visual Studio now required. Almost all platforms which used VS2015 before now require Visual Studio 2019, so please ensure you install this if you haven't already and also check your GMS2 Preferences paths are now correct, otherwise you will have errors when building YYC platforms/UWP/consoles. More information and a link to the Required SDKs can be found further down this page or on the Help menu inside GMS2 itself.

We also squeezed in two new console exports - Microsoft Xbox Series X/S and Sony PlayStation 5! If you are already approved for consoles these will appear in Target Manager as normal.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes, so please do read the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Ubuntu IDE Beta
changes: We are pleased to offer a new Ubuntu IDE beta for you to try (requires Ubuntu 20.04.n LTS) - more info on this can be found on the "How to get Betas" FAQ
Please note as per the other IDEs, we do not support virtual machine OSes and that this is the only Linux distro we offer official support for in this Beta

groups.title: Changed All IDE Input And Audio Output To Use SDL2
changes: This is a huge internal change, but you will hopefully only see that it fixes a number of minor differences in keyboard/mouse and file dragging-and-dropping support Windows IDE vs Mac IDE
Also fixes a few issues with copy/pasting clipboard contents between GMS2 and other applications - especially in the Mac IDE

Note for specifically Windows 7 users: the Windows IDE's legacy graphics tablet driver integration has now been removed as part of this change and we cannot guarantee that your own tablet driver is supported

However, because of that change, the IDE's startup sequence on Windows 7 is now much more reliable - if you had occasional crashes where your log ended on a line about the tablet driver, those crashes will be gone now

groups.title: Changed All IDE Rendering To Use FNA3D
changes: Again, this is a huge internal change, but you will hopefully only see that it fixes a number of minor differences in rendering between Windows IDE vs Mac IDE
Will allow future versions of GMS2 to better support users who have multiple monitors with different DPI values or dragging between a laptop screen and an external monitor, for example

Also allows us to prepare for future versions of the IDE being rendered with Metal on new macOS versions and to switch Windows IDE rendering to DirectX and avoid some GPU driver startup crash issues for some users

groups.title: Stability Fixes For When You Do Not Have Internet Access
changes: Fixed a startup crash when trying to activate runtimes if you are offline during GMS2's startup

Note that the crash above only happened when your original install failed slightly due to permission issues and so no runtime has ever successfully set itself as active in your settings files. This fix will allow GMS2 to safely start, but you will be asked to reinstall your runtimes one more time
Please see our permissions FAQ to ensure this installation works smoothly, otherwise you may continue to have some issues working offline

groups.title: Extension Editor "Injection" UI Changes
changes: The code injection panels inside the Extension Editor (Android and iOS) now rely on you passing in XML to indicate what should be injected and where, as there are now so many places gradle can inject to that adding a panel for each would have made the editor very messy

If you have projects which make use of the existing injection functionality please do make a backup before you open them the first time and then review them carefully in this version, as you might need to make changes to your setup - any issues, please send us a bug report and include a copy of your backup

Be aware that existing injection content will be updated into the new format the first time you edit any existing content, so after you make changes you would not be able to use this extension in 2.3.3-or-older again without having to remove and re-add your injection setup using the old format

Please see the manual for an updated overview of the extension editor, plus we have now merged our Helpdesk guides on how to create simple extensions for a variety of platforms into the manual so everything is in one place

summary:
2.3.3 is an important stability release for a number of different features: changes to source control to resolve Github authentication issues; support for using Android NDK 22, Android Studio 4.2, and the latest Xcode on Big Sur; optimisations for the amount of work done by the IDE when displaying your projects, reducing CPU usage; and a number of performance fixes in-game also.

At the same time, it does introduce several new features, including: the Inspector has been greatly extended to support multiple additional editors; a big change to how undo/redo worked within the IDE, giving you more flexibility and a better experience; you can now declare default values for your functions' optional arguments; and in-game you can now support two mouse thumb buttons on Desktop platforms.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes, so please do read the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

2.3.3 is an important stability release for a number of different features: changes to source control to resolve Github authentication issues; support for using Android NDK 22, Android Studio 4.2, and the latest Xcode on Big Sur; optimisations for the amount of work done by the IDE when displaying your projects, reducing CPU usage; and a number of performance fixes in-game also.

At the same time, it does introduce several new features, including: the Inspector has been greatly extended to support multiple additional editors; a big change to how undo/redo worked within the IDE, giving you more flexibility and a better experience; you can now declare default values for your functions' optional arguments; and in-game you can now support two mouse thumb buttons on Desktop platforms.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes, so please do read the release notes carefully. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Added Windows/macOS Runtimes Into The Tnstaller
changes: Depending on which IDE installer you downloaded, you now have the matching runtime for just that one platform included inside the installer
This means as soon as GMS2 is installed you can create/open projects and test them on Windows or macOS (so if you're a free licence user, then there are no further downloads required)
(If your licence allows other modules, these will still be downloaded on startup as per normal)

groups.title: Removed Git Tools From The Installer
changes: GMS2 now relies on external source control tools you point to in Preferences, rather than us shipping a specific version of the Git tools

This means you can point at your own installed-and-configured Git client and use its own authentication settings, etc. It also means your tools can easily be kept up-to-date with external changes by Github, etc.

Note 1: This does mean that if you were using source control inside GMS2 previously you will need to reconfigure your Git settings one time in Preferences before your projects are going to show as SCM-enabled!

Note 2: The Mac IDE cannot push to an online repository if your keychain has not already been pre-configured with your password, etc., so when GMS2 detects this error we have added a dialog saying this and (briefly) how to fix

groups.title: New Undo System
changes: All undo and redo actions have been changed to use a new per-asset history system, which brings a few benefits:

It's always going to be the most recent action which is undone - e.g., in previous releases if you create a Sprite, resize it in the Sprite Editor, open it in the Image Editor and add some content, then click the Sprite Editor and press Ctrl+Z it would be the resize which was undone rather than the Image Editor change. Now, focus is set back to the Image Editor and the last change there is undone (and pressing Undo again would step back through the change history for the asset as you would expect)
It's also now possible to undo a change to an asset after you have closed its editor - as above, the editor would be reopened and the change performed
If you do see any issues with undo/redo, then please do try to determine the precise steps to recreate the issue, otherwise we may need your project to be sent also with your ticket

groups.title: Fixes For High CPU Usage
changes: The last couple of GMS2 releases have shown higher-than-expected CPU usage values on some machines (particularly on Windows), and this release aims to reduce that back down again

In theory, you shouldn't see any issues and hopefully CPU usage values are considerably lower on your machine now - if you find your usage numbers have for some reason gone up noticeably, then please do file a ticket about this and include a project which shows the issue on your machine

changes: Should make importing and previewing sounds more reliable
There was also a specific bug fix for Add Existing importing a single sound from another project could in some cases cause GMS2 to crash

groups.title: Additional Inspector Editors
changes: These are: Objects (and individual object instances inside the Sequence Editor), Notes, Scripts, Sequences (and instances of), Shaders, and Tilesets

If you multi-select items, then be aware only the relevant shared fields will be inspectable

groups.title: Added Default Values Support For Your Function Arguments
changes: Allows you to declare default values for your arguments at the time you define them, so you can skip having to declare them each time you later call the function later

A very simple example could be defining CreatePlayer(myWeapon, myLives = 3, myHealth = 100) and then later being able to call CreatePlayer(“Sword”), knowing that myLives and myHealth will use the defaults

Note that the order you define your arguments in must be matched when later calling the function: defining CreatePlayer(myLives = 3, myHealth = 100, myWeapon) and then calling CreatePlayer(“Sword”) would give you a bug in your game as myLives would equal “Sword”

You can also turn on the extended syntax help in Preferences and add your argument defaults into your JSDoc info for the function, and this will allow you to see that your functions have optional arguments and what they will default to

groups.title: Added buffer_set_used_size()
changes: In previous GMS2 releases, using vertex_buffer_create_from_buffer() to create a buffer in an extension would require you to call buffer_fill() also, otherwise the runner didn't know the buffer had data
Now you can use this function in combination with buffer_get_size() to quickly and accurately fix this issue - e.g., "buffer_set_used_size(myBuffer, buffer_get_size(myBuffer));
As always, see the new manual page for this function for more info

groups.title: Added font_get_info()
changes: Returns a structure that describes all the information known about the given font whilst in-game
Note that whilst you can edit this struct, is is purely for your own info and any changes made will not affect the font
“undefined” is returned if the font requested does not exist
See the new manual page for this function for more info

groups.title: Added sprite_get_info()
changes: Very similar to the font one above, this gives a struct of all the information that the game knows about a given sprite (and each of its frames)
Again, see the new manual page for this function for more info

groups.title: Added Side Mouse Buttons Support (Desktop and Web)
changes: Added support for two new thumb buttons on mice on these platforms
mb_side1 and mb_side2 constants have been added for detecting when these have been used

groups.title: Itch.io/Newgrounds Window-focusing Changes
changes: Games will now set focus on launch and then will check if the game is still in focus after each mouse click

groups.title: Reverted To 2.2.5's Behaviour When Setting image_index Values Manually
changes: 2.3.3 will no longer clamp decimal image_index values larger than the actual number of frames in your sprite until the following frame (which is what 2.2.5-and-older did, but changed in 2.3.0)
This means code you may have to check if image_index >= image_number or <= 0 will now work as per 2.2.5 again

However, be aware that if you are setting image_index yourself you will now not get any Broadcast Messages for the frames between the old value and the new one you just set - these frames are skipped entirely

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: Building Projects: [Android YYC] The NDK 22 installation check now finds your install correctly when starting builds
Building Projects: [HTML5] Added additional iframe focus-detection code in response to Itch.io/Newgrounds changes (see above)
Building projects: [iOS YYC] Mac IDE fix for the error 'tell app \\"Xcode\\" to quit' which appears for some users
In-Game: Sequences now create their object instances at their correct x/y values rather than creating them all at 0x0 and then quickly moving

In-Game: Sequences within another sequence no longer flicker when played in-game if both sequences are set to loop

In-Game: [VM] Fixed a memory leak when assigning strings to multi-dimensional array indexes and then clearing the array
In-Game: [YYC] Fixed a "trying to index variable that is not an array" error when reusing same name for a local array inside and outside a with()
In-Game: [YYC] Calling a function and not passing a parameter now returns the same "undefined" value VM does, rather than a unique "unset" error

In-Game: [macOS] Fixed that collisions between objects both set to precise masks did not work correctly

In-Game: [HTML5] No longer rounds the value of image_index following the changes to image_index in 2.3.2
In-Game: [HTML5] Cameras will now keep following the designated follow object even after game_restart() is used when in a different room
In-Game: [HTML5] Function parameters that use the same name as built-in variables no longer become undefined
In-Game: [HTML5] Is now consistent with all other platforms in that undefined < 0 is "false"
In-Game: [HTML5] Games no longer crash if you have a Colour Multiply track without a parameter key
In-Game: [HTML5] Loading a saved struct from a buffer no longer makes the buffer unchangeable thereafter
In-Game: [HTML5] Rotation is now applied correctly for Sprites on an Asset Layer
In-Game: [HTML5] Setting an array inside a static function will no longer crash the game with "Cannot Set Property '0' of 'Undefined'"
In-Game: [Android] Games no longer crash when loading/unloading audio groups if using Dynamic Asset Delivery also
In-Game: [Android] Games no longer crash when playing sounds if using Google Dynamic Asset Delivery and compressed OGGs
In-Game: [UWP] Audio no longer stops playing on the Xbox if headphones are removed or attached while game is running
In-Game: [HTML5] array_resize() now sets all cells to "undefined" rather than "0", as other platforms already do
In-Game: audio_start_recording() no longer gives a small memory leak each time you call it
In-Game: ceil() now gives the same result on YYC as it did on VM when the value passed to the function contains >15 decimal places
In-Game: draw_text_ext() does not wrap on all standardised break-able whitespace characters
In-Game: draw_text_transformed_color() or draw_text_ext_transformed_color() no longer cause misaligned glyphs when rotating this text
In-Game: ds_grid() passing a negative value no longer causes an error suggesting a large amount of memory has been allocated
In-Game: font_add() loading DejaVu Sans Extra Light no longer causes the game to crash
In-Game: game_end() in a global-scope script now actually closes the game on startup, as might be expected
In-Game: game_restart() no longer causes a game crash under certain conditions
In-Game: [HTML5] grid_resize() with 0,0 values no longer causes a game crash

In-Game: [HTML5] layer_sequence_speedscale() increasing the speed of a sequence no longer crashes the game

In-Game: sprite_collision_mask() changing a sprite's bounding box type now affects the results gained by later calling sprite_get_bbox_mode()

In-Game: [HTML5] script_get_name() always returns undefined
In-Game: view_camera in a startup script no longer causes a silent crash
In-Game: [Windows] window_set_size() no longer causes the game window to briefly fill white on some GPUs

summary:
2.3.2 is all about performance. It introduces new Nine Slice support for your sprites, allowing you to create nicer-looking menu screens and HUDs in a quick and easy way; adds the new animcurve library containing preset curves you can use to very quickly and easily apply common behaviours to your animations; offers new IDE and manual languages so you can work more quickly and easily in a language you prefer; changed the Tutorials button on the Start Page to now open our Learn website, so we can offer new tutorials, fixes, and more localised versions at a faster rate. It also removes a few memory/performance bugs in the IDE, reduces compile times (in the majority of cases), improves the garbage collector for a little more in-game performance and a lot more stability, and also smoothens FPS values when on Windows (particularly for those of you with high-refresh monitors). And if you want speed and ease when passing your macOS games around, try the new .dmg export for non-App Store builds.

There are of course also a number of important bug fixes and a few changes, so please do review the whole of the release notes thoroughly and make yourself aware of these. See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Nine Slice Support
changes: Nine Slices allow you to scale your sprites to stretch in a more controllable and smarter way, by keeping your corners at a fixed scale and stretching the bits in-between

The Sprite Editor has a new Nine Slice panel where you can now enable this, and of course this new capability carries through into your game, where you can later manipulate the sprite at runtime should you wish
Introduces the new functions sprite_nineslice_create(), sprite_set_nineslice() and sprite_get_nineslice(), as well as a number of in-built variables
Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ runtime also when building your project

groups.title: AnimCurve Library
changes: We have added a new library of preset curve types you can apply to your Bezier curves to automatically add points or change ease in/out values and easily add effects like "bounce" or "elastic"
Presets can be applied to a whole curve or between selected points only
Also added a ? button for opening the relevant manual page onto each of the AnimCurve Editor, the AnimCurve Library window, and the Sequence Editor

groups.title: New IDE and Manual localisations
changes: We have now added Brazilian-Portuguese, Chinese, and Russian translations into the IDE, the installer, and also the online/downloadable versions of our manual
As a reminder, you can change your IDE language in Preferences > General Settings and your Help language in Preferences > General Settings > Help
Our www.yoyogames.com site also supports these languages and includes links to the translated manuals

groups.title: Use Your Default Browser For Our New Tutorials
changes: Continuing our drive to use external browsers for all website functionality and thereby improve usability, as well as reduce the GMS2 install size, the Start's Page's Tutorials will now open our website in your default browser outside GMS2

https://www.yoyogames.com/en/tutorials is our newly-updated and expanded website dedicated to tutorials and other learning resources, which allows filtering by proficiency level and also by the topics you're interested in

Please note that we do not recommend continuing to use our old Start Page/Marketplace tutorials in 2.3.2+ IDEs, as these will have formatting issues and some problems with links to videos - these old assets will be removed from the Marketplace in future

groups.title: Mac DMG Export Package
changes: If you are not building for the App Store, then when you click the Create Exe button now you will be given the choice of wrapping your new app in a .zip (as always) or a .dmg installer
A new Game Option has been added to control the dmg installer's background image, and it will reuse the same icon as the game app uses
Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ runtime also when building your project

groups.title: Live Updating of the Colour Picker values
changes: Now, when spawning a colour picker in any applicable editor, you will be able to tweak your colours and see these apply in the main editor straight away - no more having to apply the colour change to see the update and then re-open the picker to make tweaks

groups.title: New Sequence Playback DND Nodes
changes: Along with a small stack of fixes for other DND issues in this release, we have added some new nodes for controlling playback of your sequences:
"Sequence Get Length", "Sequence Get Head Position", and "Sequence Set Head Position"
Note this feature requires a 2.3.2+ runtime also when building your project

groups.title: Misc Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: AnimCurve Editor: Added clearer UI messages to show when a curve is in an error state or invalid/not suitable for the operation you are trying to perform, which should allow you to quickly fix or pick a suitable replacement curve

DnD Editor: Changed "Start Following Path" node's Relative->Absolute checkbox label, so now it matches how GML handles this functionality and also how recent GMS2 versions have actually handled the value in-game

Local Packages: Fixed that collision events with assets not actually in the package were not imported because there was no matching second object to tie the event to and so the event information was lost from the object which was imported, so GMS2 will now create a new empty object of the required name in order to preserve the collision event information

Project Load: Changed "IdReferences which are not found" compiler log warnings to be actual errors for you to resolve, rather than allowing the projects to keep building with broken in-game information. However, the error message now outputs what the exact issue is and where to fix it, so it's much easier to resolve your errors than in previous releases

summary:
2.3.1 is an evolution of the new Sequences functionality introduced in 2.3.0 - we have added Bezier curve support as well as improved the dopesheet and curve editor workflows to allow you to more accurately control and develop your Sequences, introduced new functions to scale/rotate your sequence and to query information from your curves, and enabled broadcast messages in all Sprites so they can trigger events in-game. There are also a lot of very important fixes for project conversion/import, an updated version of Mono is now required by the macOS IDE to fix some issues with projects not building on some Macs, and multiple fixes for configs and extensions throughout the IDE and when building projects.

On the runtime side, as well as a large number of in-game bug fixes this release introduces Windows x64, Ubuntu ARMv7, UWP multiple-architectures-in-one-package, and Apple Silicon-compatible macOS output types. There are important fixes for garbage collection and configs support in-game, which fixes a number of issues with games crashing in 2.3.0. Please note that 2.3.1 also updates SDKs/external tools for some of the platforms, so you should be aware of this when updating and building projects.

See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Project Conversion Fixes
changes: Lots and lots of project conversion issues have been fixed (and a number of you have recieved fixed copies of your projects already, so they're not listed below), however the vast majority were due to one of the following four reasons:
1) The default texture/audio groups disappearing from the old project during the conversion process (the same issue which was affecting our own tutorials)
2) Corrupt views referencing resources multiple times (so the project may have had issues in 2.2.5, saying it couldn't find files, etc.)
3) DnD Scripts referencing multiple resources in unhandled ways
4) Amazon's Game Options not upgrading properly from very old values to current ones

If your project previously failed to convert in 2.3.0 (and we haven't already sent you a fixed copy), please try it again now. If it still fails, then please file a bug ticket and send us the project .yyz/.zip

groups.title: Bezier Curves
changes: Added a new curve type in the Curve Editor - Beziers allow you to ease in/out of curve points and fine-tune your animations

Also made a number of improvements to manipulating curves used as position tracks on the Sequence Editor canvas - such as live preview/updating of the canvas area as you modify your curves and the ability to modify your bezier handles on the canvas itself

groups.title: Dopesheet Curve Editor
changes: Further improving curve-editing, you can now edit your embedded curves right in the dopesheet within the Sequence Editor - toggle to the curve editing mode and make your changes to see the canvas update
Added a "Height of Anim Curve Track in Dopesheet" Preference so you can choose whether you want your curves to be double-height in the Dopesheet

groups.title: Snappable Dopesheet
changes: And finally for curve-editing and the Sequence Editor, you can also now snap the Dopesheet to the top, bottom, left or right edges of the Sequence Editor ...or you can pop it out into its own floating window
Closing or "resetting" a floating Dopesheet will restore it back to the default (bottom) snap
Each Sequence has its own snap/floating setting so that you can do things like float the dopesheet for one sequence and see it alongside the dopesheet for another

groups.title: Sprite Broadcast Messages
changes: 2.3.0 added the ability for a sequence track to fire off Broadcast Messages, and now 2.3.1 brings the same functionality to all sprites
You add the message as a moment on the Sprite Editor timeline and then this fires in-game when that frame is reached

groups.title: Room Manager Tools
changes: The Room Manager window has now been extended so you can more easily move your rooms around when you have lots of them you need to manage - some UI tweaks, new send to top/bottom buttons, plus the ability to add groups
Note that grouping the rooms has no effect on their order - this is still always performed top-to-bottom

groups.title: Multiple New Package Formats
changes: Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device you are targeting for that build)
UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

groups.title: Removed The English Manual From The Installer
changes: As more of you are using GMS2's localisation capabilities and choosing to work in your native languages, we have now removed the English manual from the GMS2 install to save a reasonable amount of download size and install space requirement
The first time you access the manual inside GMS2 you will be asked if you want to download a local copy and work offline or if you're happy continuing with the online manual
If you want to download the manual later on, or want to change your manual language, then you can do this via Preferences > General Settings > Help
Be aware also that as well as manual.yoyogames.com (English), there is now also manual-de (Deutsch), manual-fr (Française) and manual-es (Español)

groups.title: Misc Other Changes
changes: Changed the default sorting method used when importing a project to be Custom, so the Asset Browser order matches how the project looked before

Changed the code-folding on { to be on the function line always, so that you don't get a dangling { as in 2.3.0 - also added a Preference to disable code-folding on { for those who only want to fold via regions

Added a new Preference for whether you want changing the filtering of the asset browser to immediately re-expanded the groups or not (that the asset browser always expanded all groups each time you created an asset while the filter is active has been fixed)

Have had to slightly change the Mac IDE keys for managing Bookmarks, as the old ones clashed with macOS hotkeys and so caused issues - setting a bookmark is now CMD+CTRL+[0-9] and jumping back to it later is CMD+[0-9]
Within the Sequence Editor, you can now create Moment functions using the name you set in the text box, rather than having to create and then rename
Added a Preference to edit the boiler plate comment shown at the top of a new Script Resource (or to turn it off if you want)
Added a timeout to debugger connections - so now GMS2 will abort the build and show a "Are you perhaps firewalled?" if the debugger takes too long, rather than waiting indefinitely
File > My Account will now use your default browser, rather than opening a browser workspace tab inside GMS2
Lots of missing translations for 2.3.0 features have now been added, along with the translations for the new stuff in 2.3.1

Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)
Removed some redundant arguments from buffer_get_surface(), so you will need to refactor any code using this function

groups.title: Multiple Garbage Collection Improvements
changes: Added support for incremental collection and changed the collector to use this, which means the workload will be spread over multiple frames and avoid spikes
Fixed an issue where some garbage objects were being considered multiple times, so less work is now being done
Changed how garbage objects are generated, so now far fewer items are created/considered and so there is even less work being done
Added weak references support via weak_ref_create(), weak_ref_alive() and weak_ref_any_alive(), so you can further control how garbage is handled
Changed the colour used for garbage collection in show_debug_overlay() to be blue, so now you can more easily identify when it's working
And fixed several in-game crashes and performance bugs, as shown in the bugs list below

groups.title: Support for Android 11
changes: Added support for Android API 30 and NDK 21
Also updated the Gradle version GMS2 will use during your builds to target v6.1.1 (please note that you will need internet access for your first Android build, as Gradle will download its updates!)
Note that GMS2 games can now be run in PiP mode on Android 11 over the top of other apps, but do not support having other apps open over the top of them
Added support for Android Dynamic Asset Delivery in your bundle builds (it doesn't apply to .apk, which have APK Expansion already) - note that this is not limited to Android 11

groups.title: Support for recent Apple platform releases
changes: Added support for XCode 12, iOS and tvOS 14
Added .bundle and Cocoapods support for iOS extensions
Re-enabled hardened runtime support to be on by default for macOS builds
Also fixed various memory-management issues specific to macOS and removed some debug spew

groups.title: Multiple New Package Formats
changes: Windows x64 runner support (toggled via Game Options > Windows)
ARMv7 packages for Ubuntu (GMS2 works this out dynamically depending on the architecture of the device your targeting that build)
UWP multiple architectures in one package (part of the Create Exe button process)
Should you have one, you will also find GMS2 itself and macOS games now run fine on your Apple Silicon developer-testing Mac

If you have issues with your projects running fine in the "regular" versions of any of these but in the "new" versions they are incorrect, then please do file a bug ticket and send us the .yyz/.zip copy of the project (give us a download URL if the project is larger than 20MB)

groups.title: Important Changes To Be Aware Of
changes: Various platform SDK requirements have changed since 2.3.0, so please do check your setup againt the Required SDKs FAQs if you now have build issues.

game_save() has been fixed to save all the new internal variables introduced in 2.3.0, plus your member variables - however, this results in a format change compared to 2.2.5, and so existing 2.2.5-and-older game saves are not going to work with game_load() now

ds_list_write() has been fixed to write out the correct formatting version number required for 2.3.0+ strings. Unfortunately, this does mean whilst strings from 2.2.5 and older will be read correctly in 2.3.1, if that ds contained an array then strings from 2.3.0 builds will not - if you had released a version of your game using 2.3.0 and you had array data as part of the string you will unfortunately need to use a 2.2.5 version of your game to read your 2.3.0 data then re-save the string. It does also mean that if you intend supporting some players using older versions of your game (e.g., built with 2.2.5), then they would not be able to read a string created by a player using a build made in 2.3.1.

There are a few functions which previously returned 0 to indicate a success even when the manual says they didn't return anything. These have now all been changed to return "undefined", as 0 was causing issues where some users had code incorrectly checking the return of these functions and then trying to perfom an action, so they were usually accidentally calling the function at index 0 - which is typically camera stuff. If you suddenly find your game is now erroring due to trying to run an "undefined" function, see if this change applies to your code and refactor accordingly.

groups.title: Misc Other Changes
changes: Fixed an issue on some platforms where a switch() which contained only a default (no other cases) could cause issues
Changed window_set_fullscreen() so it now uses the same delay that Alt+Enter has always used, in order to stop black screens when toggling to fullscreen in some cases
Added functions to scale and rotate sequences - see layer_sequence_angle(), layer_sequence_xscale(), and layer_sequence_yscale() in the manual
Added a function to get the channel index from an anim curve - see animcurve_get_channel_index() in the manual

Added the $ symbol as a new accessor for structs (Which does mean if you have existing code for assigning HEX values to a variable then make sure you haven't wrapped this hex value in []s, as this would cause a compile error now)

summary:
2.3.0 is a huge new release which brings multiple new asset types and editors, significant quality-of-life changes and productivity gains to the existing editors, and a new project format to handle all these new additions. There is a lot changed in this release, so please do read all the release notes carefully and follow the link to our detailed guide to changes in 2.3.0.

Please also be aware that opening an existing project in 2.3.0 the first time will ask you to convert the project and save it out again with a new name. This is because the project format has now been changed quite extensively. You will not be able to open newer-style projects in 2.2.5 or older, and similarly 2.3.0 does not allow you to set 2.2.5 or older runtimes as active.

See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: The Asset Browser
changes: A major overhaul and replacement for the resource tree - order your assets however you want them, no more fixed per-resource groups
Add tags to your assets to filter your browser, but also get these tags in-game and react to them during gameplay
Use the new Quick Access menu to order your rooms, set assets as favourites, save searches, and modify your game options

groups.title: Sequences asset type
changes: Create animations, cutscenes, and control gameplay in this new resource type with its powerful new editor
Call functions during standard events (like Create, Step, Destroy) and also on-demand at any point on your timeline as a Moment
Send on-demand Broadcast Messages which can be picked up by any instance in your room

groups.title: Animation Curves asset type
changes: Control the assets in your sequences with curves, so you can do things like change position, blend colours, control audio volume, and tweak your animations

groups.title: The Inspector
changes: Modify a sequence's asset properties in a fast and easy new way

groups.title: A brand new manual
changes: A clean new look and much better search tools
Also opens in your browser for maximum readability and productivity (note that it's still an offline copy served from your GMS2 install)
Includes a brand-new beginners guide, perfect for getting to grips with GMS2

groups.title: Misc
changes: The Sprite Editor and Image Editor both now have a new preview bar where you can manipulate your frames
Rewrote the folder watcher to be more efficient and robust
Made the Go To tool able to search Preferences and Game Options for matches to your search terms
Added code-folding on all opening curly braces
Updated Game Options iOS to use the newer splash screens and icons setup that current Xcode wants
Made some tweaks to Marketplace asset-creation (along with adding support for 2.3.0+ assets and the new project format)

groups.title: Bugs
changes: For the full list of public IDE issues fixed in this version since 2.2.5, see the Change Log
Note, however, that this is a very small list compared to the full private change log and you will no doubt find a lot of old issues have been fixed

groups.title: Scripts now contain functions
changes: A script asset is no longer limited to being just one custom function - instead, you will find a new function declaration is added whenever you create a script, and you can add your own below this and call these functions as required elsewhere in your game

Scripts are also now processed on startup, which means if you create a script which contains lines which are not wrapped in a function declaration, those lines will always run on game start, allowing you to very easily create initialisation scripts and control functionality
NOTE: You should review your scripts after importing any 2.2.5 projects in case you need to remove/tweak these function declarations so that your game initialises correctly.

groups.title: Methods
changes: You can also now bind functions to your instances and call them in a natural way

groups.title: All arrays are now 1D
changes: However, they can actually now be chained, so you can create arrays three (or more) deep if you require by chaining the declaration - e.g. array[0][0][0]
The 2D array functions have now been deprecated, but if you have these in your 2.2.5 projects they will still work due to the compatibility layer

groups.title: Sequences and Animation Curves
changes: There are new functions to allow you to create entirely new assets at runtime or to return and modify existing ones created in the IDE

groups.title: Structs
changes: You can now declare structs, which are (in very simple terms) one variable holding a collection of other variables, and create instances of these on-demand, allowing you to manage your data more clearly

groups.title: Garbage Collector
changes:
The runner now has a multi-stage garbage collector to clean up in-game memory and maintain performance
 <li>This is all automatically done for you, but there are functions to allow you to call it on-demand also and even to turn it off if you wish

groups.title: Handling exceptions via Try/Catch
changes: You can now Try() a bit of code and Catch() if it gave any errors, allowing you to hopefully recover from a bad situation
If things aren't recoverable, you can also Finally() a last bit of code before your game shows an error and ends
You can also Throw() an exception at any time, allowing you to create your own custom errors
And you can handle runner exceptions also by declaring your own unhandled exception handler

groups.title: Bugs
changes: For the full list of public in-game issues fixed in this version since 2.2.5, see the Change Log
Note, however, that this is a very small list compared to the full private change log and you will no doubt find a lot of old issues have been fixed

summary:
2.2.5 is a small but very important stability release, while we continue developing all the new features in 2.3.0.

See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.

groups.title: Updated HTTPS certificate support for the Windows IDE
changes: It's still a way off, but by the end of Q2 2020 the YoYo Account servers will have to stop supporting the older HTTPS standard currently used by the Windows IDE
(Internet server/traffic circumstances out of our control might make this sooner, but we're planning end of Q2)
This release brings the Windows IDE into line with the Mac one, and so both will continue working just fine after that date

groups.title: Fixes for the Crash Reporter
changes: Depending on the circumstances of the crash, some users saw the crash reporter itself would close before they could send us their crash log - this release fixes that
If you see the crash report screen, please do send us the report and then we can fix the underlying issue - thanks!

groups.title: Misc
changes: Fixed that showing certain font characters in various parts of the IDE would occasionally cause the IDE font to become corrupted
Fixed that on macOS the IDE was needlessly requesting permission to have GMS2 receive keystrokes from any application, not just GMS2 itself
Fixed the Code Editor so an "if" statement with an immediately succeeding semicolon now says in syntax highlighting that this would be a compiler error
Added a reminder to scroll up and read the whole compiler log (and see your Compile Errors window if one appears) to find out why your build failed, rather than only reading the last line
Removed some redundant UI for "Extension Options Files" and "Supports" from the Extension Editor

groups.title: Bugs
changes: For the full list of public IDE issues fixed in this version, see the Change Log
Thinking of reporting a bug? See the IDE's Known Issues page first

summary:
2.2.4 introduces a big update of the build toolchain to match the requirements of Android 10 and also macOS/iOS/tvOS following Apple's recent announcements - please update to this version if you're using macOS Catalina. IAP support has been greatly updated - including subscriptions support and receipt verification functionality! Plus, there has been another big push on making HTML5 games work more closely to how they do on other platforms. There have also been some changes to how and when files are created and a clean-up of some redundant game options, which should result in less confusion when working on your projects.

Please be aware there is a change to licensing, so GMS2 will say your licence format is invalid the first time you start the IDE. Simply "Retry" this prompt and log-in again to re-validate your licence. You should only see this once.

See below for IDE changes/fixes and check the Runtime Release Notes for in-game changes/fixes.
